message: Command `find /workspace/_work -type f | head -50 && echo "===" && ls -la /workspace/_work/` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
Now I understand the vulnerability. The `vcardstructured_new_from_string` function at line 59-87 of vcardstructured.c has a buffer overflow: it writes to `st->field[st->num_fields++]` without checking against `VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS` (20). If the input string has more than 20 semicolon-separated fields, it writes beyond the `field[20]` array, corrupting adjacent memory (including `num_fields` itself potentially). Then `vcardstructured_free` reads `st->field[i]` for `i < st->num_fields`, which may be uninitialized memory.

Let me check the fuzzer harness to understand what input format is expected.

<｜｜DSML｜｜>
